newsitem.title: USA: California controller pays $1.2 bln to Calpers.
newsitem.headline: California controller pays $1.2 bln to Calpers.

text.p: California's controller Wednesday repaid the state's largest pension fund more than $1.2 billion that the governor and the legislature used to balance state budgets in the early 1990s.

Controller Kathleen Connell's office said it transferred the money to the California Public Employees' Retirement System (Calpers) after the state's Department of Finance certified that California's treasury had enough money on hand to cover the giant payment.
"Finally, employer contributions that were unlawfully delayed have been restored," said Calpers spokeswoman Patricia Macht. "We're happy to get it back."
Calpers said it was still owed $300 million in interest, which the pension fund expects to receive from the state in the coming months.

A state appeals court ruled earlier this year that the governor and the legislature improperly withheld the money from Calpers in the early 1990s to balance state budgets during California's deepest economic downturn since the Depression. The state Supreme Court let the ruling stand.
California lawmakers had hoped to pay back the money over several years. But Calpers was "unwilling to offer an affordable" repayment plan, Gov. Pete Wilson said.

Wilson, a Republican, said by repaying the entire amount immediately, California taxpayers would save at least $650 million. The governor said, however, that the repayment would require state lawmakers to sharply curtail their spending plans for the 1997-1998 budget year. Funding for tax cuts and other programmes may have to be eliminated, Wilson said.

With more than $115 billion in assets, Calpers is the largest public pension system in the United States. Calpers manages retirement and health plans serving more than one million workers, retirees and their families.
